final_candidates.decision_summary: Introduces an N-linked glycan at N161-I162-S163, likely sterically blocking antibody binding while preserving local folding better than charge reversal.
Removes the N119 glycan and introduces a negative charge, likely disrupting antibody recognition with some cell-entry risk.
Reverses surface charge in a likely antibody epitope loop to weaken antibody binding without removing a large side-chain feature.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence is available and further self-review is unlikely to improve the top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: Removes a predicted N-linked glycosylation sequon and alters charge in a known neutralizing epitope loop, likely reducing 37.2D/8.9F binding without grossly disrupting GP1 folding.
Removes the N119 glycan and introduces a negative charge, likely disrupting antibody recognition, though with some cell-entry risk.
Removes a surface-exposed positive charge in a GP1 loop implicated in 12.1F/8.9F recognition; conservative size change should preserve local structure.
Creating N161-I162-S163 adds an N-linked glycan, which should sterically block antibody binding while preserving local folding better than charge reversal.
Charge reversal at an exposed GP1 residue likely disrupts antibody electrostatic contacts; may affect receptor binding but is a known escape-like substitution.
Surface charge reversal in a likely antibody epitope loop.
Charge reversal in the same solvent-exposed loop as N119, likely to disrupt 37.2D/8.9F paratope contacts while retaining loop hydrophilicity.
Charge reversal may aid escape, but the basic residue could contribute to receptor binding, lowering confidence.
Removes a negative charge near the N119 glycan site and may alter the epitope surface presented to neutralizing antibodies.
Surface charge loss may modestly alter antibody binding, but no glycan addition and uncertain epitope role.
Conservative aromatic change that may reduce antibody shape complementarity without strongly affecting GP1 folding or receptor contacts.
Conservative removal of a hydroxyl is unlikely to produce strong antibody escape.

rejection.reason: Conservative removal of a hydroxyl is unlikely to produce strong antibody escape.

history.rationale: Hydrophobic substitution in an exposed loop likely alters the 12.1F epitope surface while preserving core packing.
Hydrophobic conservative substitution is unlikely to strongly alter antibody binding.

rejection.reason: Hydrophobic conservative substitution is unlikely to strongly alter antibody binding.

history.rationale: Bulky aromatic substitution at a polar exposed position may sterically interfere with antibody binding in the N119 loop epitope.
Bulky aromatic substitution may affect receptor binding more than it improves escape.

rejection.reason: Bulky aromatic substitution may affect receptor binding more than it improves escape.

history.rationale: Alternative charge swap at the same glycosylation site; stronger electrostatic disruption but slightly higher folding risk than N119D.
Adding a positive charge at N119 is likely more disruptive to folding/receptor interaction than beneficial for escape.

rejection.reason: Adding a positive charge at N119 is likely more disruptive to folding/receptor interaction than beneficial for escape.

history.rationale: Introduces a positive charge adjacent to Y150/E151 and may weaken antibody contacts through altered local electrostatics.
Weak surface charge change with uncertain epitope relevance.

rejection.reason: Weak surface charge change with uncertain epitope relevance.

history.rationale: Removes the N119 glycan without introducing a charge, likely preserving entry better than N119D/K while still altering antibody binding.
Charge reversal at K161 may disrupt antibody electrostatics without adding a glycan.
Nearby surface position; introducing a negative charge may alter the epitope without large side-chain removal.
